newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close quiet, mixed as CANTV nears end.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close quiet, mixed as CANTV nears end.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed mixed in thin trade as investors took a breather from the domestic placement of shares in Venezuelan telephone company CANTV, traders said.

"All was slow, thin and quiet. The market was finishing off CANTV," said one trader. Small Venezuelan investors had until Friday afternoon to place their orders, while institutional investors have until Tuesday.
The market's 19-share .IBC index rose 0.81 percent to close at 5,966.75 points as 14 shares rose, 14 fell and 12 ended flat.
"We're very pleased at how people have responded," said Agustn Cangas, representative of the local lead CANTV syndicate, Santander brokers and Merinvest.
Cangas said demand for the shares had crescendoed through the week after a slow start.
"Venezuelans always come through at the last moment, in the last hour, on the last day," he said.
Despite the hurry, some 50,000 Venezuelans managed to place orders for some $105 million worth of shares, according to official figures, with demand particularly strong in the capital.
"The prospectuses arrived late ... so did the share order forms, but nevertheless it all went well," said one broker.
In the wider market, some 13.9 million shares traded, worth 2.67 billion bolivars ($5.7 million).
"The market could come alive next week after the CANTV placement is through," said another broker.
Among widely held stocks Electricidad de Caracas firmed 7.50 bolivars to end at 537.50. Foods group Mavesa rose 2.00 bolivers to close at 43.00.
Steel company Sivensa rose 9.00 bolivars to close at 339.00. U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers started Sivensa as a buy Friday.
